description.narrative:
Svenska ambassaden har fått en förfrågan av ZOA och YMCA att finansiera projektet "Peacebuilding and Reconciliation through Community Dialogues II" i Liberia med 11 600 000 kronor under perioden 2021-2022.
Huvudsyftet med stödet är stärka konfliktlösning och försoning på lokal nivå, samt att förbättra individers psykosociala välmående och familjedynamik och att stärka jämställdhet på familjenivå. Insatsen omfattar dessa områden:
* Förbättrad mental hälsa och psykosocialt välmående
* Förbättrad social sammanhållning och medborgerligt förtroende
* God sammhällsstyrning/good governance
* Stärkt medborgardeltagande
* Ökad tillgång till information

ZOA and YMCA have applied to the Swedish Embassy for funding of 11 600 000 SEK to carry out the project "Peacebuilding and Reconciliation through Community Dialogues II" in Liberia during the period 2021-2022.
The intervention aims at strengthening conflict resolution and reconciliation initiatives at community and county level, while improving individual well-being and family dynamics, including more gender equal relations at the household level. The project is centered around these areas:
* Improved mental health and psychosocial well-being * Improved co-existence and civic trust * Good governance * Increased levels of civic engagement * Increased access to information
*Outcome 1: Improved psychosocial well-being and enhanced interpersonal relations within families and the community
*Outcome 2: Local leaders and government officials adhere to and act upon good governance principles
*Outcome 3: Improved civic participation and positive engagement with local government
*Outcome 4: A peaceful and safe school environment is established for students to reach their full potential
Outcome 5: Increased capacity of YMCA to independently implement similar projects

The overall objective of the project is to strengthen conflict resolution and reconciliation at community and county levels in Liberia. Through the implementation of community-based, bottom-up approaches in which project participants increase their self-awareness, learn more positive behaviours and are able to meaningfully connect to each other, this project contributes to strengthening peaceful conflict resolution and reconciliation at local levels.
The specific objective of this project is to strengthen social cohesion and civic trust within and between communities and between population and local government in five counties in Liberia. Community-based methodologies are implemented for strengthening peace, social cohesion and civic engagement as well as civic trust and enhancing good governance principles, including transparency, accountability, participation and inclusion.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution
Promotion of mental health and well-being

description.narrative:
ZOA successfully implemented all planned activities, and as a result strengthen conflict resolution and reconciliation at community and county levels in Liberia. The contribution included a component to strengthen the capacity of YMCA Liberia which was very successful and YMCA Liberia signed an agreement with the Embassy in 2023. The Embassy has assessed that YMCA has built their capacity through this support and are prepared for direct funding from the Embassy. YMCA has also been successful in the implementation of the Community Leadership Forums and Peace Clubs, and shows great potential to continuing strengthening social cohesion through these efforts.
Examples of results include: - 6840 persons (M: 4668, F:2172) participated in Community Based Sociotherapy (CBS) groups. - 74 % of participants in CBS for leaders reported on better connections with citizens and 70 % understands the benefits of good governance. - Local leaders who participated in CBS for leaders saw a change in sharing of information, listening to others, more women in leadership positions and making community laws. - 85 % of participants in CLFs reported an increased level of successful collective action - 75 % of participants in CLFs reported increased instances in which citizens inputs influenced decision-making. - 230 persons (M: 166, F: 64) including local duty bearers, women and young people, participated in CLFs where they agreed on and follow through on action plans addressing key issues they had identified in the communities. - 1 000 students engaged in peace clubs
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
